scope: Experimental Linux native letter-case sequencing and opt-in timing. Not generic text-completion or latency acceptance.

environment.guest: Verified original Harmattan inputs in private disposable snapshots
environment.transport: Private files and owned QMP stdio; no listener

actual_native_input.source: OS desktop automation through the Godot window, then bridge-owned guest touchscreen input
actual_native_input.before: The unchanged timing implementation with diagnostics inserted only L from the 16-key Linux works AaZz burst; later requests were rejected or expired after repeated Shift.
actual_native_input.after: The same 16-key burst displayed Linux works AaZz; all 16 key events were accepted. A subsequent space and ABC displayed Linux works AaZz ABC and saved in the Notes list.
actual_native_input.focus_interruption: A pending X was cancelled after its contact had already reached the guest. Focus return and a new b displayed Xb, with no X replay.

cancelled_sequences.63: Release cancelled by the immediately following Quit

rapid_delete_and_retype.baseline_lifecycle: All three processes exited 0 through native Quit; zero graphics faults/rejections and workers joined.

known_failures.separate_graphics_path: A longer baseline Notes new/cancel/Escape sequence stopped at the strict GPU gate with ten FBO/renderbuffer call faults. Those wire operations are missing from the current render dispatcher; current-context ambiguity is not resolved by those logs. This keyboard change does not repair or bypass that gate.

host_suite.clang_retry: The one affected test passed with the previously installed official LLVM 19 toolchain, zero skips.

timing_limits: The successful 16-key burst took 6.941 seconds from first bridge service start through last acknowledgement. It is a bounded correctness observation, not a throughput comparison.
Queue timing starts at the first identity-checked bridge read, before full event validation; completion is a bridge acknowledgement, not visible text completion.
Godot and Python process clocks are separate; do not subtract their raw monotonic values.
Nested phase times must not be summed.
No physical input, display scanout, macOS runtime or general keyboard-layout validation was performed.
